claims.statement: For a nonzero proper finite cone K, indecomposability is equivalent to every identity-dominated positive endomorphism being cI (0≤c≤1), and to identity spanning an extreme ray of Pos(K). Its unique indecomposable direct-sum projections P_a give [0,I]_K={Σ_a c_a P_a:0≤c_a≤1}. Hence every finite positive instrument with Σ_y T_y=I on all K has T_y=Σ_a c_ya P_a with stochastic columns: it reweights summand masses and retains internal normalized states. For one fixed such instrument, group summands by equality of their complete outcome columns. A nonempty closed convex C in the normalized base is stable under all defined outcomes iff each extreme point lies within one group base, equivalently C is the convex hull of its group intersections, equivalently C is closed under group conditioning. Its smallest stable closed convex hull from x is the convex hull of the occupied group-conditionals. Intrinsic cone positivity does not preserve a fixed ambient passive-likelihood contract.

Fixed-instrument stability uses one fixed complete instrument and every defined outcome at every x in nonempty closed convex C⊆B. Groups identify equal full vectors (c_ya)_y, not one outcome coefficient or one-state probabilities.
